items.title: The Four Reliances Set Up Against Four Kinds of Person

items.zh: 補特伽羅四種別故。謂因諂詐補特伽羅差別故，建立初依；因順世間補特伽羅差別故，建立第二；因住自見取補特伽羅差別故，建立第三；因聞為極補特伽羅差別故，建立第四；
items.en: Because there are four different kinds of person. That is: because of the flattering-and-deceitful kind of person the first reliance is established; because of the world-conforming kind, the second; because of the kind who dwells in grasping their own views, the third; and because of the kind for whom hearing is the utmost, the fourth.

items.zh: 因其諂詐，說法是依，非數取趣。要與彼論分別決擇，方證正智；非唯由彼現威儀故。
items.en: Because of such flattery and deceit, it is taught that the Dharma is the reliance, not the person. One must debate and discriminate with them to confirm right knowledge — not [trust them] merely because they present a dignified bearing.

items.title: The Four Reliances Across the Four Times of Practice

items.zh: 謂佛宣說補特伽羅及與諸法，唯法是依，非數取趣。世俗言辭不應執故。法又二種，謂文及義。唯義是依，非文。何以故？不應但聞即為究竟。要須於義思惟、籌量、審觀察故。
items.en: When the Buddha teaches of persons and of dharmas, the Dharma alone is the reliance, not the person — because conventional expressions should not be clung to. The Dharma is again of two kinds: the letter and the meaning; the meaning alone is the reliance, not the letter. Why? Because one should not take mere hearing as final; one must think over, weigh, and closely examine the meaning.

items.zh: 佛所說經，或有了義，或不了義。觀察義時，了義是依，非不了義。世尊或時宣說依趣福、不動識。為往善趣故；或時宣說四聖諦智，為向涅槃故。於修法隨法行時，唯智是依，非識。
items.en: Among the sūtras the Buddha taught, some are of definitive meaning and some of provisional meaning; when examining the meaning, the definitive is the reliance, not the provisional. The World-Honoured One sometimes taught the consciousness that inclines towards merit and towards imperturbable karma, so that beings might reach the good destinies; and sometimes taught the wisdom of the four noble truths, so that they might head towards nirvāṇa. When practising the Dharma in accord with the Dharma, wisdom alone is the reliance, not consciousness.

items.zh: 略於四時失不失故，建立四種補特伽羅。謂得法時、住持時、觀察義時、修法隨法行時。依四時故，建立四依。
items.en: In brief, because of failing or not failing at four times, four kinds of person are set up — the time of attaining the Dharma, the time of retaining it, the time of examining its meaning, and the time of practising the Dharma in accord with the Dharma. On the basis of these four times, the four reliances are established.

items.title: Attention and Object: Opening the Ground's Major Analysis of Meditative Method

items.zh: 復次，已說安立，當知於此靜慮等中，作意、所緣二種差別。作意差別者，謂七種根本作意及餘四十作意。
items.en: Furthermore, the establishing [of the ground] having been explained, one should know that within these dhyānas and the rest there are two further distinctions: attention and object. … As for the distinctions of attention: there are seven root attentions and, besides these, forty attentions.

items.title: The Seven Root Attentions: The Engine of the Meditative Path

items.zh: 云何七種作意？謂了相作意、勝解作意、遠離作意、攝樂作意、觀察作意、加行究竟作意、加行究竟果作意。云何四十作意？
items.en: What are the seven attentions? The attention that knows the marks, the attention of resolute conviction, the attention of seclusion, the attention of delight-in-gathering, the attention of investigation, the attention of the consummation of means, and the attention of the fruit of the consummation of means.

items.title: The Forty Attentions, Listed in Full

items.zh: 謂緣法作意、緣義作意、緣身作意、緣受作意、緣心作意、緣法作意、勝解作意、真實作意、有學作意、無學作意、非學非無學作意、遍知作意、正斷作意、已斷作意、有分別影像所緣作意、無分別影像所緣作意、事邊際所緣作意、所作成辦所緣作意、勝解思擇作意、寂靜作意、一分修作意、具分修作意、無間作意、殷重作意、隨順作意、對治作意、順清淨作意、順觀察作意、力勵運轉作意、有間運轉作意、有功用運轉作意、自然運轉作意、思擇作意、內攝作意、淨障作意、依止成辦所行清淨作意、他所建立作意、內增上取作意、廣大作意、遍行作意。
items.en: That is: attention on the teaching-letter; attention on the meaning; attention on the body; on feeling; on mind; on phenomena; the attention of resolute conviction; the attention of the real; the trainee's attention; the adept's attention; the neither-trainee-nor-adept attention; the attention of full knowledge; of active severance; of what is already severed; attention on an object that is a discriminated image; on an object that is a non-discriminated image; on an object at the limit of the thing; on an object of the task accomplished; the attention of resolute discernment; the attention of stilling; the attention of partial cultivation; of full cultivation; the uninterrupted attention; the earnest attention; the conforming attention; the counteracting attention; the attention conducing to purity; the attention conducing to investigation; the attention that runs by forced effort; that runs with interruption; that runs with effort; that runs spontaneously; the attention of discernment; the attention of inward gathering; the attention that purifies the obstruction; the attention of the purity of conduct accomplished in reliance; the attention established by others; the attention grasped by inner ascendancy; the vast attention; and the all-pervading attention.

items.title: First Explanations: The Three Wisdoms, the Four Foundations, and the Constructed vs. the Real

items.zh: 緣法作意者，謂聞所成慧相應作意。緣義作意者，謂思、修所成慧相應作意。緣身、受、心、法作意者，謂修念住者，如理思惟身等作意。
items.en: Attention on the teaching-letter is the attention associated with the wisdom born of hearing. Attention on the meaning is the attention associated with the wisdom born of reflection and cultivation. Attention on body, feeling, mind, and phenomena is the attention of one cultivating the foundations of mindfulness, soundly contemplating the body and the rest.

items.zh: 勝解作意者，謂修靜慮者，隨其所欲、於諸事相增益作意。真實作意者，謂以自相、共相及真如相，如理思惟諸法作意。
items.en: The attention of resolute conviction is that of one cultivating dhyāna who, according to his wish, augments the marks of things by attention. The attention of the real is the attention that soundly contemplates phenomena through their self-mark, their common mark, and their mark of suchness.

items.title: Trainee and Adept Attention: Why Even a Noble Trainee's Wholesome Mind Is Still Contaminated

items.zh: 有學作意略有二種。一者、自性，二、在相續。自性者，謂有學無漏作意。在相續者，謂有學一切善作意。如有學作意，當知無學作意二種亦爾。
items.en: The trainee's attention is, in brief, of two kinds: first, by its own nature; second, as it occurs in the continuum. By its own nature: the trainee's uncontaminated attention. In the continuum: all the wholesome attention of a trainee. As with the trainee's attention, know that the adept's attention is likewise twofold.

items.title: Ordinary Attention, and the Three Attentions of Knowing, Severing, and Having-Severed

items.zh: 非學非無學作意者，謂一切世間作意。遍知作意者，謂由此故遍知所緣、而不斷惑。正斷作意者，謂由此故俱作二事。已斷作意者，謂斷煩惱後所有作意。
items.en: The neither-trainee-nor-adept attention is all worldly attention. The attention of full knowledge is that by which one fully knows the object yet does not [yet] sever affliction. The attention of active severance is that by which one does both things at once. The attention of what-is-already-severed is all the attention that occurs after affliction has been severed.

items.title: The Four Object-Attentions: Insight, Calm, the Limit of the Thing, and the Task Accomplished

items.zh: 有分別影像所緣作意者，謂由此故，修緣分別體境毘鉢舍那。無分別影像所緣作意者，謂由此故，修緣分別體境奢摩他。事邊際所緣作意者，謂由此故，了知一切身、受、心、法所緣邊際；過此更無身、受、心、法。
items.en: Attention on an object that is a discriminated image is that by which one cultivates insight taking as its object a mentally-discriminated field. Attention on an object that is a non-discriminated image is that by which one cultivates calm taking as its object [that same] mentally-discriminated field. Attention on an object at the limit of the thing is that by which one comes to know the outer bound of all objects — body, feeling, mind, and phenomena — beyond which there is no further body, feeling, mind, or phenomenon.

items.zh: 所作成辦所緣作意者，謂我思惟如此如此，若我思惟如是如是，當有如此如此，當辦如是如是；及緣清淨所緣作意。
items.en: Attention on an object of the task-accomplished is: "as I contemplate thus and thus, and as I contemplate so and so, there will come to be thus and thus, and there will be accomplished so and so"; and it is also the attention taking a purified object.

blocks.text: Today completes the four reliances and then opens the treatise's major analysis of meditative method: **attention** (作意) and its **object** (所緣). The seven root attentions are the engine of the meditative path; the forty attentions describe every way attention can be turned in practice. The *Śrāvakabhūmi* develops them at length; here they are introduced.

subs.head: The four reliances against four persons

blocks.text: Each reliance guards against a kind of person:

items: **The Dharma, not the person**: against those who trust a teacher's bearing and reputation. Master Cháng Bǎi: "one needs an eye that discerns the Dharma; see whether this person has realised non-discriminating wisdom, not just his outward dignity."
**The meaning, not the letter**: against those who cling to words.
**Definitive, not provisional, sūtras**: against those who take expedient teachings literally.
**Wisdom, not consciousness**: against those who rely on ordinary discriminating cognition.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi maps them onto practice: at the stage of hearing, rely on the Dharma and the meaning; at reflection, on definitive meaning; at cultivation, on wisdom.

The treatise now gives "the major analysis of meditative method". Venerable Miào Jìng's image for **attention** from Day 54 returns: "like a gatekeeper; when a guest outside wants to see someone, the gatekeeper goes to fetch them". Attention decides what the mind meets.
The **seven root attentions** (七種作意), which structure the progress from desire-realm mind to the first dhyāna and beyond:

items: the attention that **knows the marks** (了相): understanding the faults of the lower level and the qualities of the higher;
**resolute conviction** (勝解): imaginatively holding that understanding;
**seclusion** (遠離): beginning to cut the afflictions of the lower level;
**delight-in-gathering** (攝樂): joy in the progress, and disgust with what remains;
**investigation** (觀察): testing whether affliction is truly gone. Master Cháng Bǎi: "in meditation, deliberately make some object of desire appear in the mind and see how the mind reacts";
**consummation of means** (加行究竟): the final cutting;
**fruit of consummation** (加行究竟果): the dhyāna attained.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng adds: "Cutting afflictions requires attention of the real; imagination only subdues them." The second attention prepares; the third and sixth actually cut.

Forty kinds of attention follow, beginning with attention on the letter (with wisdom from hearing) and on the meaning (with wisdom from reflection and cultivation); then the four foundations of mindfulness; constructed and real attention; and attentions of trainees and adepts.

Master Cháng Bǎi on the trainee: a stream-enterer has cut conceptual self-grasping but not innate self-grasping, so even their wholesome worldly attention is still "contaminated". Progress is real but not yet complete.

Four attentions concern the object: **insight**, **calm**, the **limit of the thing**, and the **task accomplished**. Master Cháng Bǎi on calm's "non-discriminated image": it still discriminates, but repeatedly on one object, as in counting breaths. On the limit of the thing: knowing the bounds of body, feeling, mind (the eight consciousnesses), and phenomena (the fifty-one mental factors); beyond these, nothing further is to be found.

quiz.q: What are the four reliances the Buddha taught?
options: the Dharma not the person; the meaning not the letter; definitive not provisional sūtras; wisdom not consciousness
quiz.why: "First, the Dharma is the reliance, not the person; second, the meaning is the reliance, not the letter; third, the sūtras of definitive meaning are the reliance, not those of provisional meaning; fourth, wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: this wisdom is uncontaminated non-discriminating wisdom that sees ultimate truth.

quiz.q: The first reliance is set against flatterers; one must debate rather than trust bearing. How does Master Cháng Bǎi say to discern them?
options: have a Dharma-discerning eye — check whether he has realised non-discriminating wisdom, not just his outward dignity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "One needs an eye that discerns the Dharma — see whether this person has realised non-discriminating wisdom, not merely their outward bearing." Venerable Miào Jìng: not because they look dignified, are famous, or have many followers.

quiz.q: The four reliances follow four times of practice. How does Master Cháng Bǎi map them onto hearing, reflection, and cultivation?
options: at hearing, rely on Dharma and meaning; at reflection, on definitive meaning; at cultivation, on wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "At the stage of hearing-wisdom rely on the Dharma not the person, on meaning not letter; at reflection, on the definitive not the provisional; at cultivation, on wisdom not consciousness." Venerable Miào Jìng: "consciousness" is that inclining towards merit and imperturbable karma; "wisdom" is the four truths.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the seven root attentions?
options: knowing marks, resolute conviction, seclusion, delight-in-gathering, investigation, consummation of means, fruit of consummation
quiz.why: "The attention that knows the marks, the attention of resolute conviction, the attention of seclusion, the attention of delight-in-gathering, the attention of investigation, the attention of the consummation of means, and the attention of the fruit of the consummation of means." Venerable Miào Jìng: no meditation, worldly or transcendent, does without them.

quiz.q: What simile does Venerable Miào Jìng use for "attention" (作意)?
options: a gatekeeper — when a visitor asks for someone, the gatekeeper goes to fetch them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Like a gatekeeper: when a guest outside wants to see someone, the gatekeeper goes to contact that person" — attention directs the mind towards its object. Master Cháng Bǎi: without attention, even with sound faculties and a present object, no cognition arises.

quiz.q: Between resolute-conviction attention and attention of the real, which cuts afflictions, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only attention of the real cuts afflictions; imaginative conviction only suppresses them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Cutting afflictions requires attention of the real; imagination won't do — it only subdues them." The text: conviction "augments the marks of things by attention"; the real "contemplates phenomena through their self-mark, common mark, and mark of suchness."

quiz.q: A trainee's wholesome attention "in the continuum" — why is a trainee's worldly good still contaminated, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: trainees have cut the conceptual self-grasping but not the innate
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "A trainee has cut the sixth consciousness's conceptual self-grasping but not innate self-grasping, so their worldly wholesome attention is still contaminated." By nature, a trainee's attention is uncontaminated; an adept's is uncontaminated in both respects.
